descriptions.panel:
Manage respondent SAMPLES — synthetic personas and paid recruits.

        Pick `action`:

        • action="create" — build a synthetic panel (AI-generated personas).
          Required: name, num_respondents, research_objective.
          Optional:  context (e.g. real distributions from `demographics`),
                     audience.
          The panel is saved to your team's library; the returned panel_id
          works with action="run", chat(), and the Flashpoint app.

        • action="run" — run an existing synthetic panel from your team's
          library through a survey.
          Required: panel_id (from action="create", list_my_panels, or the
                    app), survey_id.
          Returns a job_id immediately — runs take minutes to tens of
          minutes. Poll with action="status".

        • action="create_and_run" — convenience: build a fresh synth panel
          and run it through a survey. Same job_id + status flow as "run".
          Required: name, num_respondents, research_objective, survey_id.

        • action="status" — progress of a run / create_and_run job.
          Required: job_id. Returns status ("running" | "completed" |
          "failed" | "interrupted"), stage, progress (0–1 within the
          stage), message, and when finished the result or error.
          Poll about once a minute; don't wait on a single call.

        • action="recruit" — real PAID respondents from Prolific / Dynata.
          Required: survey_id (price quote is per-survey) OR `request`
                    (free-text catalog browse, e.g. "what Prolific filters
                    are available?").
          Optional: provider, num_respondents, audience.
          Delegates to the surveys agent's quote → confirm → checkout flow.
          NOTHING is charged without an explicit confirm step on a follow-up
          call threaded by conversation_id.

        Routing is by action only — no overloading on which args are set.
        Worker queue names are unchanged (create_panel,
        synthetic_panel_take_survey, delegate_to_surveys).
descriptions.tool_survey:
Run the Flashpoint surveys agent — the single entry point for
        ANYTHING survey-related.

        Hand it a natural-language brief and it runs its own multi-turn
        loop (planning + ~150 internal tools) to take the next steps
        itself. You do NOT chain individual operations, and you do NOT
        route survey work to `chat()` — this one tool owns the full
        lifecycle:
          • Plan & research: clarify the objective, research the market /
            audience / competitors, propose a blueprint before building;
            start from a template or save a survey as one.
          • Design: author / edit questions in 20+ types (single, multi,
            grids, ranking, MaxDiff, conjoint / CBC, image compare,
            spatial allocation, thermometer, sliders, open ends, contact
            form, AI-moderated interview); blocks + rotation /
            randomisation, answer lists, skip & display logic, piping,
            loops, URL variables, redirect URLs, derived values,
            exclusive options, data validation.
          • Quotas & sample sources: quota cells, least-fill, quota
            sheets, progress / reconcile / export; BYO sample sources
            (per-vendor links + redirects), first-party and custom panels.
          • Languages: add survey languages, machine-translate, review or
            set individual translations.
          • Validation & QA: surveycheck (logic prover), publish readiness,
            DSL validation, QA rounds with findings, walk a respondent
            path, field report, client review link.
          • Launch & lifecycle: publish, pause, resume, complete, clone,
            transfer; version history, compare, restore, undo.
          • PAID recruitment (Prolific / Dynata / Cint): browse filters
            and markets, get a price quote, then on your confirmation get
            a secure checkout link. Just ask — e.g. "recruit 5 Prolific
            respondents for this survey, quote first". NOTHING is charged
            without an explicit confirm step (see the confirm pattern
            below). Panel status / pause / resume after launch.
          • Distribution: email lists + templates, invitations, reminders,
            send to a panel, send reports.
          • Data quality: speeders, straightliners, quality summary,
            exclude responses, generate test data.
          • Analysis & exports: frequencies, crosstabs with stat tests,
            NPS, open-end themes, AI summaries / key takeaways; conjoint
            analytics (market simulator, willingness-to-pay, sensitivity,
            segments, product optimizer, share link); CSV / XLSX / DOCX /
            PDF exports; results dashboard.
          • Collaboration: comments on questions, resolve threads.

        Interactive cards (plan, approval, results dashboard, conjoint
        simulator, checkout) render in the Flashpoint web app, not here —
        the text reply carries the substance, and every MCP conversation
        is also visible at app.flashpoint.ai afterwards.

        ALWAYS thread `conversation_id` across related calls (build →
        recruit → analyze) so the agent keeps full context of the survey
        it just worked on — pass the value returned by the previous call.

        Confirm pattern (money / destructive actions): the agent will NOT
        perform a consequential action on the first ask. It replies asking
        you to confirm; relay that to the user, then call again on the SAME
        `conversation_id` with their confirmation (e.g. "confirm") to
        proceed. This is how approval works on the direct path — there is
        no UI card to click.

        Args:
            brief: What you want done, in natural language — a build spec,
                an edit, a recruitment request, an analysis ask, an export,
                a confirmation, etc.
            survey_id: Pass to act on an existing survey; omit to create a
                new one.
            conversation_id: Pass the value returned by a previous call to
                continue the same thread (REQUIRED to keep context across
                build → recruit → analyze and to satisfy a confirm step).
                Omit on the very first call and the server mints one
                (uuid7).

        The agent may take 60–600s. Returns the worker's result blob
        (typically includes the relevant `survey_id`) with the
        `conversation_id` echoed back so follow-up calls thread.

result.summary:
Panel 'Stress-Tester trial panel': 10/10 personas generated
Age range: 26-44, median 36
Gender: Male: 5, Female: 5
Income: 75-100k: 4, 100-150k: 3, 50-75k: 3
Top locations: Austin, USA (1), Columbus, USA (1), Chicago, USA (1)
Top roles: UX Designer (1), Operations Manager (1), Public Relations Manager (1), Healthcare Administrator (1), Automotive Service Advisor (1)
COMPOSITION: sampled to real population marginals on gender. Invented by the generator, not sampled: age, race, education, income. Do not describe the panel as matching Census data on those. independence — marginals matched, correlation not modelled. Caveats: gender: no Census counts for this panel; used the US adult split.

notes: gender: no Census counts for this panel; used the US adult split

tool_survey.brief:
Using ONLY the free synthetic panel 'Stress-Tester trial panel' I just created (AI personas, no paid recruitment, no payment), run a one-question survey.
Show each respondent this exact text: "Earn 4.25% APY on your savings with no monthly fees and no minimum balance."
Question (single choice, 1-10): How appealing is this offer to you personally? Answer with a single whole number from 1 (not at all appealing) to 10 (extremely appealing).
Field it to the synthetic panel now, then return every respondent's numeric answer as JSON: {"responses": [..], "mean": .., "n": ..}, plus the survey_id.

result.final_text: Survey is built. Now handing off to the orchestrator to run the synthetic panel through it.
